video_caption: The video begins with an animated shot of Earth orbiting the sun, with the text "The earth is orbiting around the sun" appearing on screen. This transitions to an animation of a massive solar flare erupting from the sun, accompanied by the text "Suddenly The sun sends one of the strongest solar storms towards the earth." The scene then shifts to a city on a coastline as a colossal tsunami wave approaches, and the text "earth undergoes a lot of changes on its surface" is displayed. This is followed by an aerial view of a city engulfed in widespread fires and explosions, with buildings collapsing, and the text "Widespread fires in cities." An animated sequence shows a solar flare striking Earth, followed by Earth's atmosphere glowing and reacting to the impact, while a voiceover describes the potential for "highly destructive effects on humans and the Earth indirectly." The animated Earth then loses all its city lights, indicating power outages, with the text "Power and internet outages for several months or even years" appearing. Further animations depict Earth's surface cracking with glowing fissures, followed by shots of large icebergs in an ocean and a boat being overwhelmed by a massive wave. Text appears on screen: "rising Earth temperatures melting polar ice caps tsunamis hundreds of meters," indicating the consequences of global warming and massive waves. The video shows a flooded city with partially submerged skyscrapers and a large wave crashing over an offshore oil rig. The segment concludes with various wide shots of a desolate, destroyed city, with buildings reduced to rubble and engulfed in smoke and fire, while the text on screen expands to "rising Earth temperatures melting polar ice caps tsunamis hundreds of meters the extinction of the human race," and the voiceover warns that "the extinction of the human race could be the effects of these devastating storms."

The video opens with a fiery, turbulent close-up of the sun's surface, glowing intensely with orange and yellow hues, while a spherical celestial body, possibly Earth, is partially visible on the right edge. The text "@jasonstambo" appears briefly at the bottom left. The scene then transitions to a cityscape bathed in an ominous red-orange glow, with tall skyscrapers silhouetted against a cloudy, fiery sky. This dramatic imagery transitions again to a wider shot of a devastated cityscape, with a large, metallic-looking "2012" superimposed against a bleak, cloudy sky. Below the numbers, a sprawling urban area appears to be collapsing into a tumultuous ocean, with massive waves engulfing buildings and debris, suggesting a catastrophic event. Throughout these scenes, a blue circular logo with "BOU" in white is consistently displayed in the top right corner.

The video segment opens with a vibrant close-up of the sun, depicted as a large, fiery reddish-orange sphere with an intensely bright and textured surface. Glowing, almost molten-like areas are scattered across its surface, with darker, more intricate patterns in between. A prominent, exceptionally bright solar flare erupts from the right side of the sun, arching upwards and spewing material into the dark expanse of space. In the top right corner, a white "BOU" logo is visible. Briefly, at the bottom center of the screen, the timecode "00:01" appears, followed by "© 150".

The video begins with a fiery red-orange shot of the Sun, showing intense solar flares and eruptions, with text overlays "© ESA" and a "BOU" logo. This transitions to a futuristic, sci-fi scene where a holographic projection of a man in a business suit appears and disappears from a circular platform, suggesting time travel, with text "Science Time". An animated sequence then depicts a solar storm erupting from the Sun, traveling past a satellite, and impacting Earth, illustrating the phenomenon. The scene shifts to historical elements, showing a person with light skin writing with a quill pen by candlelight ("© OnTen"), contrasting with a modern electricity pylon against a cloudy sky. Further historical context is provided by a close-up of a lit oil lantern ("© OnTen") and two people handling large ice blocks in a dark room ("© OnTen"), representing past methods of light and refrigeration. An antique telegraph machine is then shown, with a hand pressing its key in two different close-up shots, one with a lantern in the background ("© OnTen"), highlighting early communication technology. The video then returns to space with an animated Earth, showing expanding green auroras over Europe ("© NASA Video"), followed by striking real-world images of the Aurora Borealis over snowy landscapes and water ("© OnTen"). A world map highlights Mexico in red, illustrating the wide reach of the auroras. This is succeeded by more images of the northern lights above trees and a pier ("© OnTen"). The narrative shifts back to the Sun with an animated, violent solar flare ("© NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center"), then a map of Canada with Quebec highlighted in red, indicating the location of a significant power outage. Industrial electrical transformers are shown in an outdoor setting and an aerial view of an electrical substation ("© OnTen"), representing modern power infrastructure. The impact of a power outage is dramatically shown at night, with a brightly lit house suddenly going dark ("© NBC"), followed by a city skyline experiencing a widespread blackout ("© NBC"). The video then depicts another animated fiery sun with a planet in front ("© Skydiver Entertainment"), and a powerful solar flare erupting from the Sun's surface ("© whatif!"). This leads to a shot of the International Space Station orbiting Earth, followed by a large satellite dish, emphasizing modern technology reliant on space. A person using a smartphone with a glowing red light ("© whatif!") and an animated GPS satellite orbiting Earth ("© whatif!") are shown. The control room of a flight director is then visible, with multiple screens displaying navigation data and a large screen showing Earth and a satellite, with "FLIGHT DIRECTOR" text visible. A pilot's hands are seen adjusting controls in an airplane cockpit, followed by views from inside and outside an airplane experiencing distress, suggesting a potential crash with passengers in panic, and the plane falling from the sky ("© Paramount Pictures", "© Summit Entertainment"), demonstrating the catastrophic potential of a widespread GPS failure.

The video opens in a control room where a man with glasses and a headset sits facing a large screen displaying a rocket launch and the text "FLIGHT DIRECTOR," with other smaller screens showing data. This transitions to close-ups of a fiery, orange-red sun with large solar flares erupting from its surface, sometimes displaying "NASA." An animation follows, showing the sun emitting a massive yellowish coronal mass ejection (CME) that travels towards and engulfs a small, dark planet resembling Earth. The scene then shifts to a white background showing Google search results, with queries like "Will solar storm hit Earth in 2025?" and snippets mentioning a solar maximum around July 2025 and a powerful solar flare. This is followed by a sequence of YouTube video thumbnails and titles, all speculating about a "Solar Maximum" or "Big Solar Storm" in 2025 causing an "Internet Apocalypse." After more fiery sun visuals and abstract energy flows, an animated dark planet is shown being hit by solar emissions, followed by another close-up of a sun with a large arching solar flare. The Google search results reappear, now including news articles with headlines like "Solar storms are increasing, but don't lose sleep over an 'internet apocalypse.'" and "Sun to reach Solar Maximum by 2025, likely to cause complete global internet outage." A specific article from space.com is highlighted, titled "Yes, solar storms are increasing, but don’t lose sleep over an ‘internet apocalypse.’" with a subtitle refuting "Non-existent NASA warnings." The video then shows a man with a beard and dark curly hair, wearing a black t-shirt, appearing distressed as he looks at his phone while leaning on a shelf, before throwing his phone down in frustration. This leads to a shot of a person in a dark hoodie sitting at multiple computer screens in a "Matrix"-like environment with green digital streams, with "SCIENCE TIME" visible. Three men in white shirts are then seen typing on computers in a similar setting, followed by an overhead shot of hands typing on a keyboard. The video concludes with a close-up of hands typing on a laptop, where the screen displays a chat interface from chat.openai.com/chat, showing a code generation request and response, set against a background of flowing digital code.

The video segment opens with a close-up of hands typing on a laptop, followed by an animation of Earth in space surrounded by floating words like "Propaganda," "Perceptions," "Promote," "Views," "Influencing," and "Fake News" on a dark background, implying the spread of information. This transitions to a webpage displaying an article about the sun, showing a large image of the sun with active flares in orange and red hues, and text indicating that the peak of the solar cycle is now expected in mid-to-late 2024, instead of July 2025. The scene then shifts to an office where a Black man in a blue shirt points at a computer screen displaying code, talking to a White woman with dark hair who is seated at a desk with multiple monitors, also showing code. This is followed by a screen displaying YouTube comments from users expressing concern about the release of "GTA 6" (Grand Theft Auto 6) in relation to the solar activity news, with comments like "Wait no gta 6 for several months or this video is a joke" and "New fear unlocked: Dying before GTA 6." An animated logo for "GRAND THEFT AUTO VI" then appears, showing "VI" in purple and pink with palm tree silhouettes, and the text "COMING 2025" (English: Coming 2025). The video then shows a dark view of Earth from space with visible city lights, notably over North America, followed by an aerial shot of a bustling beach and city skyline with a turquoise ocean filled with jet skis, a yacht, and dolphins. Another view from space shows vibrant green and purple aurora borealis over Earth, with a part of a space station visible in the foreground. A close-up shot of a person with red painted nails holding a white PlayStation 5 controller is shown. Finally, the video concludes with two post-apocalyptic scenes: one of a ruined Sydney Opera House partially submerged in murky water with a dystopian city background, and another showing a bent and broken Eiffel Tower in a desolate, ruined city landscape under an orange-brown, dusty sky, suggesting widespread devastation. Throughout the video, a "BOU" logo is consistently displayed in the top right corner.

The video opens with a night scene of a highway filled with stationary cars, people standing outside their vehicles, suggesting a traffic jam or breakdown. This transitions to an aerial view of Earth at night, showing bright city lights across continents, which then progressively dim and disappear as the planet rotates. Next, a person in a dark hooded jacket runs through a smoky, debris-filled landscape with fires burning, indicating a disaster. This is followed by close-ups of hands typing on a keyboard, with programming code visible on two computer monitors, and then hands texting on a smartphone. Gold dollar signs rain down and settle on a reflective surface, symbolizing wealth. The scene shifts back to Earth, now bathed in sunlight, with a glowing network of lines and dots overlaid, representing global connectivity. A close-up of actor Nicolas Cage shows him looking distressed, after which the lights across North America on Earth slowly fade to black. An aerial view of a vibrant, lit-up city at night abruptly darkens as all lights go out. The video then shows an aerial view of a sewage treatment facility, followed by clean water pouring into an open hand, and an empty, brightly lit hospital corridor with a medical gurney. People are seen walking with luggage in a busy indoor public space, followed by a point-of-view shot of a shopping cart moving through a colorful grocery store produce aisle. A well-lit gas station at night with cars pumping gas is shown. A man in a hospital gown stands in a dark room with a single operating light, opening a cabinet. The city lights again go out. A banana peel is shown decaying over time, with text overlays indicating "day 6", "day 10", "day 15", "day 19", "day 23", and "day 28", illustrating food spoilage. A chaotic street scene with people fighting and a military presence transitions to an aerial shot of a crowded bridge where a helicopter crashes, highlighting pandemonium. An animated blue world map with glowing white lines connecting various regions depicts a global network. The final scenes show scientists or technicians in a dimly lit control room, wearing headsets and monitoring large screens, one displaying a satellite image of Earth. This is followed by an animation of a dark red planet orbiting a bright, swirling star, and finally, a close-up animation of the sun emitting powerful solar flares. Throughout the video, logos like "NBC", "Summit Entertainment", "OnTen", "what if!", and "Movi/cal" appear in the corners, indicating source material or production.

The video begins with a close-up of a person wearing brown gloves carefully connecting numerous white wires to small golden components on a sophisticated, multi-layered metal device, possibly a quantum computer. This transitions to a focused man with glasses and a beard, also gloved, intently examining similar wiring, followed by another shot of the complex device itself. Next, a black rectangular power switch labeled "POWER" (with "110" partially visible below) is shown in the off position. The scene then shifts to an animated visualization of the sun emitting a large, yellowish coronal mass ejection towards a crescent-shaped Earth in dark space ("© NASA Goddard"). This is followed by several electrical engineers in hard hats and safety vests walking across a gravel path at an expansive outdoor electrical substation with many power lines and transformers under a clear blue sky. A detailed, hand-drawn scientific graph with mathematical equations and text such as "UNCOUPLED BASIS: | β1>| β2>" and "COUPLED BASIS: | β1>| β2> | M1>| CSCO:" is displayed on a blackboard-like surface. A person in a suit is then seen from behind, gesturing at a vast, multi-screen control room display filled with various blue and red data visualizations, graphs, and a spinning globe. The video shows an animated view of Earth from space, initially dark, then revealing bright city lights across its surface. This is followed by a dramatic, hazy scene of four silhouetted figures watching an orange sunset or sunrise over a body of water. A powerful visual from a movie then depicts a colossal wave engulfing the partially collapsed Golden Gate Bridge, with people frantically running away from the destructive surge on a rocky shore ("© Warner Bros. Pictures"). The focus shifts to a close-up of a person's hands with bright red nail polish holding a white PlayStation 5 controller, its blue light glowing. An animated, fiery sun with intense solar flares and coronal loops is then shown in vibrant detail ("© NASA"). The segment concludes with a dark, ominous shot of a city skyline with tall buildings, some appearing damaged, under a stormy sky with lightning flashing in the distance ("© Netflix").

The video opens with a wide shot of Earth from space, showing its blue oceans and green landmasses against the dark, star-filled void. A white rocket with a long, thick smoke trail is seen launching from the planet's surface, ascending upwards. In the top right corner, a purple logo with white letters reads "BOU." The scene then transitions to a closer aerial view of Earth, where a massive, bright white and pink plume of smoke or debris is rising vertically from a point on the Earth's surface, extending high into the atmosphere above a landscape of water and land. The "BOU" logo remains in the top right corner, and the text "Igor Kryan" is briefly visible at the bottom center of the screen.
